purpose: Release queue activity when its last GEM binding disappears, so replacing a business path does not consume stale queue capacity.
root_cause: Native update_queue_bindings removed deleted GEMs from gem_queue_bindings but retained their previously selected queues in configured_priority_queues. paths_bytes then counted these unreferenced old queues as active alongside replacements. A target T-CONT could be reported full despite a GEM having just been deleted.
concrete_reproduction: Create8 GEM paths using8 queues on one T-CONT, delete one GEM CTP, assign a fresh queue ME to that T-CONT, then add its replacement GEM. Old code rejects the fresh queue SET with OMCI response1/backend-28 before the hardware apply callback; after the fix the SET and replacement GEM succeed and8 paths exist again.
fix: Capture the previously referenced queue IDs before updating GEM bindings.
Remove a previously referenced queue from the active set only when no GEM binding still references it.
Keep queues explicitly configured without any prior GEM reference; keep shared queues until their last GEM reference disappears.

verification.stock_cases: Remaining references0 clears queue ownership and scheduling metadata; remaining references1 preserves the queue row.
verification.stock_scope: Actual shipped post-delete reference test and metadata writes with synthetic queue rows. Successful preceding ioctl and queue deletion are preconditions, not executed; no physical PUC proof.
verification.native_test: scripts/test_omci_queues.c linked to the freshly built production Rust static library
verification.native_scope: Real OMCI CREATE/SET/DELETE through production Rust FFI, queue-binding lifecycle and snapshot exporter. Hardware apply callback models acceptance and existing error cases. Added capacity-reuse case plus existing queue remap/rollback cases; no full tests.
verification.build_scope: Offline locked Cargo build of changed OMCI library only, including cortex-a55 aarch64-unknown-linux-musl static library; isolated output directory.

limits: The reproduced failure is a false-ENOSPC (-28) from software queue accounting. It is not proof of the peer -110 hardware timeout cause or the approximately50-second ACTP restart.

Original deletion can also clean other unused queues through feature-dependent paths. This change fixes retention of formerly referenced queues; complete feature-hook lifecycle equivalence is not claimed.
No optical XGPON test, full suite, firmware build, deployment, commit or push.
